chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Salama, who said:

A man recited to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was listening, certain phrases from the Quran that were not according to what the people were reciting. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Stop this recitation! Recite as the people recite, until the Qaim (peace be upon him) arises.'

So when the Qaim (peace be upon him) arises, he will recite the Book of Allah (Exalted and Majestic) according to its precise limits, and he will bring out the Mus'haf (codex) which Ali (peace be upon him) had written.

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) brought it out to the people when he had finished compiling and writing it, and said to them: 'This is the Book of Allah (Exalted and Majestic) just as Allah revealed it to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and I have gathered it from the two Tablets.'
So they said: 'It is that which is with us, a comprehensive Mus'haf containing the Quran; we have no need for it.'
So he said: 'By Allah, you will not see it after this day of yours ever! It was incumbent upon me to inform you when I had gathered it, so that you might recite it.'

key_terms.اللَّوْحَيْنِ: The two Tablets, referring to the divine source or original records from which the Quran was compiled
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim (the Awaited Imam), referring to Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمُصْحَف: The codex or compiled book of the Quran
key_terms.حُرُوفاً: Phrases or letters, indicating specific variations in recitation
key_terms.عَلَى حَدِّهِ: According to its precise limits/standard, indicating the complete and unaltered form

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Mus'haf of Ali (peace be upon him) and the Qaim's recitation according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia doctrine of the 'Ghaybah' (occultation) of the authentic, divinely preserved Mushaf of Ali ibn Abi Talib, which contains the complete Quran with its original exegesis and variations. Imam al-Sadiq instructs the companion to adhere to the common recitation (Qira'at) used by the majority until the rise of the Qaim, emphasizing that the people's rejection of Ali's Mushaf at the time led to its concealment from public view. This narrative underscores the belief that the current Quranic text, while authentic, is not the complete, unaltered codex preserved in its entirety by the Imams.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Salim Bin Salama who said,

‘A man recited to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and I was listening, certain phrases from the Quran, not being upon what the people are reading it. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Stop from this recitation! Recite it just as the people are reciting it as until the rising of Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup>.

So when the Qaim<sup>asws</sup> does arise, he<sup>asws</sup> would recite the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic upon its limits, and he<sup>asws</sup> would bring out the Parchment which Ali<sup>asws</sup> had written’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> had brought it out when he<sup>asws</sup> was free from (compiling) it, and writing it. So he<sup>asws</sup> had said: ‘This is the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majesty just as Allah<sup>azwj</sup> had Revealed it upon Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’; and he<sup>asws</sup> had gathered it from two Tablets.
So they said, ‘It is that which is with us, a comprehensive Parchment, in which is the Quran. There is no need for us with regards to it’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You will not be seeing it after this day of yours, ever! But rather, it was upon me<sup>asws</sup> that I should inform you all when I<sup>asws</sup> had gathered it, in order for you to be reciting it’.
en.sarwar: 23. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Hashim from Salim ibn Salamah who has said

the following: “Once, a man read before abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) certain letters from the Holy Quran, while I was present, which were not like those that people read. Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said, ‘Stop this reading. Read as people read until the one who will establish Divine Authority on earth will come.
When he will come, the book of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will be read upon its limits.

He then brought the copy of the Holy Quran that Ali (a.s.) had written and said, ‘Ali (a.s.) brought this to people when he completed writing down the Holy Quran in one copy and said to them, “This is the book of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, as Allah had revealed upon Muhammad (a.s.) and I have written it in one copy from two tablets.”
They said, ‘With us there is the comprehensive copy of the Holy Quran. We do not need it.’
He then said, ‘By Allah you will never see this from today on. It was necessary for me to tell you after I completed writing it down so you can read.’”
